A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoDirector and contain readable text, figures, tables and equations. V1 includes supplementary material; v3 incorporates its preliminaries into Section 3.1 but omits the remaining supplement. The supplied documents support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-editing results, comparisons with four baselines, a nine-participant user study, and qualitative ablations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains the original comparative experiments and user study and additionally reports quantitative component-ablation results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The core STDG, multi-frame null-text optimization, and self- and cross-attention control procedures retain the same formulations. Omission of supplementary pseudocode and mask-processing details reduces documentation but does not establish an actual algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both describe the same 75 text-video editing pairs sourced from DAVIS, MotionClone, TokenFlow and online platforms, covering people, animals and objects. Foreground and background editing remain represented. Omitted supplementary examples do not establish a change to the stated dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 6 retain the same four comparators: Flatten, RAVE, TokenFlow and Video-P2P. Newly cited StableVideo and Slicedit are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: The stated resolution, 16-frame setting, AnimateDiff backbone, guidance parameters, evaluation metrics and nine-participant ranking protocol remain unchanged. Table 2 quantifies existing ablation variants using existing metrics without specifying a revised evaluation design.

E4.justification: V3 adds quantitative evidence for six component variants in Table 2, complementing the retained qualitative ablations in Figures 7–9. Conversely, it omits supplementary Figure I's shared-null-text applicability analysis and Figure II's SAM2-versus-SAM2-plus-ellipse mask robustness comparison. This substantially changes the supporting analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Mean user-study ranks remain unchanged, and the new ablation table continues point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: All Table 1 values and the main qualitative results are retained. Table 2 adds a substantial numerical ablation grid; for example, the variant without STDG reports 89.23% motion smoothness and 19.09 masked PSNR. These are newly reported results, not improvements over v1. Supplementary analysis outcomes and additional editing examples in Figures I–VI are omitted.

T1.justification: V1's explicit mathematical task definition, Vo = D(Vi | G, (C, Ce), R), is omitted with its original Section 3.1. The diffusion preliminaries are relocated from the supplement, and the proposed method's equations remain substantively unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about direct T2V-based editing, the three principal components, and superior accuracy, fidelity, motion smoothness and realism. The added trajectory-control wording makes an existing claim more explicit without expanding its scientific scope.

C2.justification: V3 emphasizes editing as controlled reconstruction, but omits supplementary qualifications about shared null-text sufficing for minimally deforming objects, fine segmentation masks destabilizing editing, and approximately 16 GB additional memory consumption versus Video-P2P. The main text still acknowledges the memory-related 16-frame restriction.

D1.justification: V3 omits Algorithm I's two-stage pseudocode, instructions to combine SAM2 and ellipse masks, and the additional-memory disclosure. These are substantive reproducibility losses despite retaining the backbone, A100 hardware, timings and guidance settings. The stated project address also changes from video-director.com to VideoDirector.com.

R1.justification: V3 adds StableVideo and Slicedit citations to related work and removes Dhariwal and Nichol's Diffusion Models Beat GANs on Image Synthesis citation associated with the omitted pseudocode. The broader positioning against T2I-based editing remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction receives localized revisions, and Section 3.1 replaces the task-and-challenges discussion with preliminaries moved from the supplement. The remaining supplementary sections are omitted, acknowledgements are added, and an affiliation is updated. Most main-text prose and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 2 while removing supplementary Figures I–VI and the Algorithm I display, substantially reducing the supplementary visual presentation. Main Figures 1–9 and Table 1 remain, with local resizing and repositioning. References change from a single-column to a two-column layout.

improvement.justification: Table 2 strengthens quantitative support for the component claims, and relocating preliminaries improves main-text accessibility. However, v3 loses practical mask-processing instructions, pseudocode, robustness evidence and applicability qualifications. These changes materially trade stronger quantitative validation against weaker reproducibility and disclosure; the supplied PDFs do not establish a clear net quality direction.
